messages:
morgan: Heads-up — seeing prolonged Xid 31 spikes on us-west-2 gpu-batch-3. Symptoms only show up after multi-hour runs. Thinking an extended burn-run (8-12h) across the suspect nodes to try to repro. Who's available to coordinate?

leo: Can you paste a small dmesg snippet and the ECC counts? Xid 31 often points at a driver/firmware fault but could be thermal/VMMemory.

morgan: dmesg snippet from node gpu-batch-3-14:
```
[ 2345.123456] NVRM: Xid (31): 0b1103bf0 0x00000000 0x00000000 0x00000000 0x00000000
[ 2345.123459] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 2346.987654] EDAC MC0: CE error, count: 12 memory-controller 0
```
ECC cumulative on that node: CE=12, UE=0 over last 7d.

isabel: If you want to run an isolated soak, cordon+drain the node then run a daemonset stress on it. Example drain command: `kubectl drain gpu-batch-3-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

sam: For the burn: we use the same runner as before — `gpu-burner`. Suggest conf: `gpu-burner --duration 12h --pattern memrw --concurrent 2 --log /var/log/gpu-burner.log`. Can wrap in a pod: image: redwood/gpu-burner:stable, run with nodeSelector for the target node.

infra-bot: [alert] node-exporter:node-gpu-batch-3-14 thermal.junction exceeded 85C 2026-02-18T02:12:03Z

leo: Also run a light I/O stress to rule out PCIe/slot issues: `fio --name=seq-write --filename=/dev/nvme0n1 --size=1G --runtime=3600 --direct=1` on that host. If we see correlated spikes in PCIe errors + Xid, lean towards hardware.

morgan: Capacity note: us-west-2 pool has ~10% spare, so we can afford to pull 2 nodes overnight (off-peak). But Dedicated customer routes are pinned to this AZ; pinging solutions to confirm no SLA impact.

isabel: Proposed acceptance criteria for returning node to service: 
- No new Xid 31/13 errors for 12h under burn + memrw test
- ECC CE delta < 5 during the soak
- no thermal throttle events > 2
If any fail, escalate to vendor RMA. Also record dmesg + nvml logs and attach to the ticket.

sam: Operational playbook steps I recommend (short):
1) Cordon+drain node
2) Start gpu-burner daemonset single-node pinned, 12h
3) Run fio for 1h on host
4) Collect: dmesg, /var/log/gpu-burner.log, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,driver_model,compute_mode --format=csv` every 10m
5) Query metrics: `sum(increase(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total{node="gpu-batch-3-14"}[12h]))` and `increase(nv_ecc_ce_total{node="gpu-batch-3-14"}[12h])`
6) If thresholds exceeded -> flag for RMA and move to replacement queue.

leo: Quick telemetry query to run from grafana console: `SELECT sum(xid_count) FROM gpu_telemetry WHERE node='gpu-batch-3-14' AND time > now() - interval '12 hours'` — helps correlate bursts.

morgan: I'll kick this off tonight at 02:00 UTC and post logs here. If the node fails acceptance, plan is to replace the card and re-run the same harness on the new card for 6h to validate.

isabel: Also add a short note in the node ticket: `observed Xid(31) + ECC CE drift, attempted 12h soak 2026-02-18, results attached` so on-call can find history.

sam: One more perf/cost note — extended burns cost ~2-3 GPU-hours per node (power + lost capacity). Tally this in the incident cost estimate so finance can track RMA-related burn ops.

morgan: Thanks — will update when run starts. If anyone wants to join the live run to watch metrics, ping me and I’ll give grafana links. :thumbsup:
